content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Sociology Student Stories Sunny Zdravkova - Equity and Diversity in Society (MA) Sunny Zdravkova - Equity and Diversity in Society (MA) Sunny Zdravkova's UWTSD Experience Hi, my name is Sunny Zdravkova. I am a mature student who is retraining to pursue my passion for social justice, belonging, and equity and advance my career. Key Stats Name: Sunny Zdravkova Course: Equity and Diversity in Society MA Hometown: Originally from Sofia, Bulgaria, but currently living in the UK. Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Sunny Zdravkova's Programme Name Experience Sunny’s Equity and Diversity in Society Experience Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD because of its flexible programme and accessibility. As someone employed full-time, it was important for me to find a course with live interactions and lectures, unlike most distance learning degrees, which are mainly online without a live tutor experience. Another reason for choosing UWTSD was the accessibility and overall inclusion of the programme. The degree welcomes individuals from all walks of life, regardless of prior education, making it easier for people from various social backgrounds to access education equally. This inclusivity was an important factor for me, as promoting equity and inclusion is fundamental to our studies. What did you enjoy outside your studies? I love spending time with my partner and my family. I also enjoy staying active, being outdoors, and travelling. Although I dedicate a lot of time to my job, I always try to find ways to relax and have some downtime. What do you hope to do when you graduate? I hope to continue learning and making a positive impact. I also aim to progress in my career and apply the knowledge and skills gained from my degree in my everyday life and work. What is your favourite thing about Equity and Diversity in Society? One of the things I appreciate most about the MA in Equity and Diversity in Society is the wide range of topics and questions we cover in our lectures and assignments. Social environments are incredibly complex, and being able to research and discuss these issues has helped me gain a broader perspective and be more understanding of the challenges faced by specific groups. This experience has been invaluable and has also improved my self-awareness and knowledge of various societal issues and challenges. What is your favourite thing about the University Campuses? I’m a distance learning and remote student. I haven’t been to the campuses yet, but I heard it’s beautiful, so I can’t wait to see it this year or the next time I visit. Did you come to UWTSD using an alternative route? Yes, I came as a mature student in hopes of retraining to pursue my passion for social justice. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Sociology Student Stories Martha Lee - Sociology (BSc Hons) Martha Lee - Sociology (BSc Hons) Martha Lee's UWTSD Experience My name is Martha Lee and I am a mature student studying Sociology and have just completed my second year at UWTSD. I stumbled across this course after attending an open day in 2022 and was immediately interested in what it had to offer. Given that much of my experience is in the care sector, I knew Sociology would broaden my knowledge and provide me with the skills to grow in the health and social care sector. Key Stats Name: Martha Lee Course: Sociology BA Previous Studies: NVQ Level 2 – Health & Social Care Hometown: Newcastle Emlyn Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Kayleigh Phillips' Programme Name Experience Martha’s Sociology Experience Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD mainly because it was close to home and as I had already lived away and was going as a mature student, I didn’t really want to venture too far. I also liked that it was relatively small, and I think this is what has made it such a good experience for me. The support network and student support are outstanding, and because our Sociology group is on the smaller side, you get to know everybody really well. What did you enjoy outside your studies? If I’m being honest, I work a fair amount when I’m not studying. However, when I’m not doing that, my favourite pastime is to go on a long walk with my dog. I haven’t really done any extracurricular activities! What do you hope to do when you graduate? At this stage, I am slightly clueless, but I am contemplating doing a masters. I genuinely thought I would never go back into education after dropping out of sixth form, but I am thoroughly enjoying my course and the experiences I have had so far. I am interested in entering either social work or the probation service, but I am still undecided. Studying Sociology has broadened my knowledge in so many different areas and has highlighted systemic issues in not only the social care sector but across all of society. While this hasn’t necessarily helped me directly in my work, it has certainly encouraged me to think about it more as well as giving me an insight into areas where I may wish to seek future employment. What is your favourite thing about Sociology? My favourite thing about studying Sociology is that we cover such a vast number of topics. It’s interesting to hear people’s perspectives and to have an open discussion in lectures (there are plenty of opportunities for a debate!). Alongside this, the lecturers are incredibly knowledgeable and supportive. Sociology covers so many aspects of people’s lives often making it very relatable, which is what makes it so interesting. What is your favourite thing about the Carmarthen Campus? My favourite thing about the Carmarthen campus is that it’s not too big! I have visited various university campuses in the past and have found it too overwhelming. Everything is within walking distance and pretty easy to find. And if you do get lost, everyone is friendly and will point you in the right direction. Did you come to UWTSD using an alternative route? Yes, I came as a mature student after being out of education for almost 10 years. Related Information Related Information Our Subjects Newsroom Previous slide Next slide

title: Ashlee Ryan-Rose - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Psychology and Counselling Student Stories Ashlee Ryan-Rose - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) Ash
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Psychology and Counselling Student Stories Ashlee Ryan-Rose - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) Ashlee Ryan-Rose - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) Ashlee Ryan-Rose's UWTSD Experience Hi! I’m Ashlee Ryan-Rose, a 29-year-old mature student at UWTSD. Three transformative years have flown by, reshaping my life in ways I never imagined. Key Stats Name: Ashlee Ryan-Rose Course: Psychology and Counselling (BSc) Previous Studies: Access to Humanities and Social Sciences Hometown: Swansea Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Ashlee Ryan-Rose's Programme Name Experience Ashlee’s Psychology and Counselling Experience What is your favourite thing about Swansea campus? One aspect I truly appreciated about the IQ campus was the outstanding academic resources it provided. The state-of-the-art facilities, well-equipped library, and abundant study areas throughout the campus created an ideal environment for learning. Also, how can I not mention the campus surroundings – whether you’d like a trip to the shops, a tasty meal, or unwind with a leisurely stroll along the picturesque coastline, the IQ campus has it all within a short distance. Why did you choose UWTSD? UWTSD not only holds a distinguished reputation but also offers a wide variety of psychology programmes that directly align with my career goal of becoming a counselling psychologist. On a personal note, maintaining a healthy balance between professional commitments, academic pursuits, and self-care is extremely important to me. Nestled in a picturesque location, the UWTSD campus is just a stone’s throw away from the serene coastline. This unique setting provides the perfect balance of nature and academia, offering an ideal environment for students to thrive and excel in their pursuits. What did you enjoy outside your studies? As an aspiring psychologist, I appreciate the importance of self-care and nurturing to maintain a healthy balance in my life-practices that proved invaluable during the demanding years of my academic journey. Outside of my studies, you can find me immersed in nature, whether that’s bike riding along the scenic coast, or marvelling at the underwater world on my snorkelling adventures off Mumbles Pier. Of course, Swansea is a foodie’s paradise, so there is always plenty of choices for exquisite restaurants to finish the day. What do you hope to do when you graduate? During my academic journey, I have been fortunate enough to acquire a wealth of knowledge and practical experience that has positioned me as a desirable candidate in the mental health sector. Within the next two weeks I will be embarking on a new professional endeavour as an LGBT+ Specialist Support Worker and Programme Facilitator for victims of domestic violence at Calan DVS. My long-term aspiration is to return to academia and continue enhancing my qualifications and experience with the aim of becoming a licensed counselling psychologist. What is your favourite thing about Psychology and Counselling? I’d have to say my favourite aspect of the BSc Psychology and Counselling degree is each amazing person that makes up the Psychology lecturing cohort that is there to support you each step of the way. As a mature student who hasn’t been in education for over a decade, I was apprehensive about returning. However, the lecturers have been incredible, taking the time to ensure I understand the material and offer guidance when I need it. Beyond lecturing, the cohort always fostered an engaging classroom environment that promoted critical thinking and discussion. Their passion for psychology and psychotherapy is inspirational! Would you recommend UWTSD and Why? The BSc Psychology and Counselling course has been truly transformative for my career trajectory. Not only has it equipped me with invaluable knowledge and resources to support individuals facing mental health challenges, but during my second-year placement, I had the incredible opportunity to put theory into practice while working alongside mental health practitioners at Swansea Mind. Due to my commitment to the cause and the knowledge imparted by the exceptional psychology cohort, I was offered a 10-month contract as a mental health practitioner. This hands-on experience has been invaluable, allowing me to directly apply the concepts learned in the classroom to make a tangible difference in people’s lives. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Psychology and Counselling Student Stories Kayleigh Phillips - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) Kayleigh Phillips - Psychology and Counselling (BSc Hons) Kayleigh Phillips' UWTSD Experience My name’s Kayleigh Phillips, I am a part-time student, studying BSc Psychology and Counselling returning to study after leaving higher education at 21. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Elis Williams-Huw - Philosophy (BA) Elis Williams-Huw - Philosophy (BA) Elis Williams-Huw's UWTSD Experience Hello, my name is Elis and I’m in my second year of studying philosophy at UWTSD. I’ve learned more than I could have expected so far and I’m very glad that I chose to study in Lampeter. After graduating I intend to do further study in philosophy and foreign languages. Key Stats Name: Elis Williams-Huw Course: BA Philosophy Hometown: Cardiff Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Elis Williams-Huw's Philosophy Experience Elis’ Philosophy Experience Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD specifically to study in a small town with a community feeling. With the size of the campus, I felt there would be flexibility that would otherwise be impossible in larger universities. What did you enjoy outside your studies? I enjoy playing football for the local team in Lampeter. I often play chess with my friends and study Japanese on my own. Did you come to the University through an alternative route? I started studying in UWTSD after 4 years of being out of education. I didn’t finish high school, so I started with the foundation year. I was fortunate to receive a lot of support from the university to ensure that I could succeed. What is your favourite thing about the Lampeter Campus? What I like about Lampeter campus is how integrated everything is. The library, lecture halls, accommodation and students’ union are all close to each other, which gives a very personal feeling environment. From the campus you can always see hills, trees and wildlife – this sets Lampeter apart as a beautiful and calm place to study. title: Rhys Price - Creative Music Technology (BA Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Rhys Price - Creative Music Technology (BA Hons)
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Rhys Price - Creative Music Technology (BA Hons) Rhys Price - Creative Music Technology (BA Hons) Rhys's UWTSD Experience Name: Rhys Price Course: BA (Hons) Creative Music Technology Hometown: Aberdare Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Rhys's BA (Hons) Creative Music Technology Experience What was your favourite thing about Cardiff campus? The best thing about my campus was the access to multiple studios. I was able to book a studio and have access to all its facilities, including all equipment and any instruments that were available. The studios also included Macs that had industry-standard software, allowing me to create music that was normally impossible with the equipment that I owned. Why did you choose UWTSD? UWTSD featured many creative aspects that other courses lacked. Typically, other courses seemed to have traditional views of music and would teach you about music analysis and theory. Creative Music Technology had a more creative and unconventional view on music, allowing the student to decide what they would want to do with their tasks. I was given a lot of freedom to express my music in my own way, and approach tasks with my own ideas What did you enjoy outside your studies? It’s fun to test out the knowledge I’ve gained by revisiting my past work and seeing how I could’ve approached things differently. Revising these songs and seeing how much they improve by using the skills gained is great for seeing how much you’ve improved as a musician. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are, and how has your course helped you in your career? Since completing my final project, I’ve been occupying myself with writing music as I did during the course. I have uploaded many songs to platforms like YouTube and Spotify and am evolving my brand as a composer to increase my audience. This course featured many lectures on branding and industry and gave insight on the harsh reality of the music industry. I was taught that choosing the correct path that a musician can follow was vital in whether you would succeed. What was your favourite thing about your course? This course provided a lot of freedom. I was never told to complete an assignment in a specific way. Since the other students on the course all had different specialties in music, the course felt like it had been adapted to help us grow in the ways we wanted by providing a diverse range of tasks. One day you could be recording a drum kit and the next you could be filming a music video or creating an instrument. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? If this course has taught me anything, it’s that there are more jobs in the music industry than you realise. You may join the course and be set on being a producer, but you never know your other interests until you try them, and those are the opportunities that will be provided for you. The practical knowledge gained from my experiences in the studios and the Mac lab is something that I couldn’t have gained anywhere else. title: Hollie-Anne Clark - Advanced Vocal Studies (MA) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Hollie-Anne Clark - Advanced Vocal Studies (MA)
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Hollie-Anne Clark - Advanced Vocal Studies (MA) Hollie-Anne Clark - Advanced Vocal Studies (MA) Hollie-Anne's UWTSD Experience Name: Hollie-Anne Clark Course: MA Advanced Vocal Studies Previous Studies: Advanced Diploma Musical Theatre (Associated Studios), MA Music (Vocal) Performance (RWCMD) Hometown: Chelmsford, Essex Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Hollie-Anne's MA Advanced Vocal Studies Experience What was your favourite thing about Cardiff campus? I really enjoyed the personal feel to the college, creating a lovely space to grow and develop your skills. There was a lot of focus on your individual craft, similar to an artist development programme and that really was a benefit. Why did you choose UWTSD? I knew of alumni and current students who had a good experience. I also was drawn to the smaller numbers on the course which allowed for more individual time. What did you enjoy outside your studies? I am a multi-faceted performer; as well as opera, I perform musical theatre, sing other styles in cabaret and act professionally. I also enjoy recording music, making music videos, and dancing in various styles! What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I have just performed and developed two vocal shows for guest entertaining on cruise lines, so that’s really exciting! One is focused on musical theatre/classical crossover and the other opera, so getting to showcase both is really great! I am also taking on the role of the Contessa in Mozart’s Marriage of Figaro this Summer, for Grimeborn Opera Festival at the Arcola Theatre. I love this role, as I performed her before, and I’m incredibly grateful to have the opportunity to perform this professionally in London for a run. I have a few festivals this summer I’m performing at too! I released my new EP Enchanted on Spotify and other platforms in February this year, and I have some new music coming soon, including writing an original too! Aside from my own performing, I also coach and teach singers, and lead a collective of performers in children’s entertainment! I’ve been lucky enough to write, direct and produce various professional shows and events including as Artistic Director of my own opera company and three pantomimes for theatre. See more of what I’ve been up to on my website www.hollieanneclark.com What was your favourite thing about your course? The personal and friendly atmosphere, and individual focus and time. And the international mix – as many students were from other countries. I would say I am where I am, because of being proactive, consistent, and persistent. But there is no destination, only the journey of seeing where my performing and skills take me, which is the adventure! It’s important to keep focused on what you want to achieve, as I believe everyone can be successful in anything they put their energy into. Doing the course at WIAV (now WAVDA), really helped me tone my skills in opera and develop vocally in a positive and encouraging environment – Dennis O’Neill was a wonderful teacher! It also gave me the tools and confidence I needed to learn roles quickly which has led to some recent successes! Would you recommend UWTSD and why? Yes – even though some of my course experience was through the pandemic, so teaching halted for a time, I found I developed a lot as an artist and met and became friends with some really great people from all over the world and made connections, so I would definitely recommend it! title: Kia Elise Breckon - Vocal Performance (BMus Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Kia Elise Breckon - Vocal Performance (BMus Hons
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Kia Elise Breckon - Vocal Performance (BMus Hons) Kia Elise Breckon - Vocal Performance (BMus Hons) Kia's UWTSD Experience Name: Kia Elise Breckon Course: BMus Vocal Performance Previous Studies: Scarborough Sixth Form College Hometown: Whitby, North Yorkshire Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Kia's BMus Vocal Performance What was your favourite thing about Cardiff campus? My favourite thing about the Cardiff campus was how central it is. It is very easy to get to and it has lots of student accommodation that is just a short walk from Haywood House. The building itself has amazing spaces that are used for lessons, masterclasses, rehearsals, and performances. As a performance student, being surrounded by the arts was so important to me, and at WAVDA that’s exactly what you get. There are so many different creative spaces near Cardiff campus including the Wales Millennium Centre which is just a short train ride away. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD because the Vocal Performance course was unlike any I had seen at other universities. UWTSD offers a unique blend of how you learn: an hour each week of one-to-one vocal coaching and a one-to-one singing lesson; lessons and projects lead by industry professionals that are still working whilst teaching; smaller classes so the lecturers are able to get to know you as a person and a performer. UWTSD has a focus on industry links and on the Vocal Performance course you build them from day one. What did you enjoy outside your studies? Outside of my studies I enjoy reading – fantasy is definitely my favourite genre. I also went to the gym before my lessons and rehearsals because it set me up with a positive mindset for the day, and I feel like I was definitely more productive. I also enjoyed meeting up with my friends who were on the Musical Theatre course. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? Now that I have finished the Vocal Performance course at UWTSD, I am going to the Royal Welsh College of Music and Drama to complete a Master’s in Arts Management. During my time at UWTSD, I found that I have a love for organisation, whether it was the programme for the Student Spotlights – which is a concert series we created on the Vocal Performance course as part of a module in second year or creating rehearsal schedules for performance projects. The course definitely helped me build on the organisation skills I already had ready for my time at RWCMD. What was your favourite thing about your course? The lecturers that I was lucky enough to be taught by were my favourite part of this course – both the HPLs and the visiting lecturers who took us for masterclasses. They are all incredible. Their passion about the arts is unmatched to anyone I’ve met before and their experiences provided me with valuable insights into the industry and inspired me. They taught me how to look after my voice, how to use it properly and how to use it in different ways which has helped me grow as a performer. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? Yes, I would highly recommend UWTSD. The university offers a unique and enriching educational experience, especially on courses like the Vocal Performance course. The experiences you get at UWTSD are incredible and I have never seen them be offered anywhere else which I feel makes the university really special. UWTSD’s focus on employability and strong industry links also provides invaluable practical experience and career opportunities. title: Elicia Axon - Acting (BA Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Elicia Axon - Acting (BA Hons) Elicia Axon - Act
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Elicia Axon - Acting (BA Hons) Elicia Axon - Acting (BA Hons) Elicia's UWTSD Experience Name: Elicia Axon Course: BA Acting Previous Studies: Queen Elizabeth High School – GCSEs and A-Levels: Performing Arts, Sociology, Welsh Baccalaureate Hometown: Carmarthen Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Elicia's BA Acting Experience What was your favourite thing about Carmarthen campus? My favourite thing about campus was the size of it. It’s not an overwhelmingly large campus – everything is quite contained in one area, so it’s super easy to navigate and move from class to class. It is like a little community and you’re able to easily interact with students on other courses. The facilities are great: I spent a lot of time studying in the library and the common areas and it was always so easy to book individual spaces for rehearsals, meetings, or study sessions. I never found myself wishing for anything the campus didn’t have. It really met my needs as a student. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose to study at UWTSD because during my audition I felt at ease the entire time. I felt extremely safe and comfortable because the campus was well laid out and signposted. The staff were so knowledgeable and passionate about the course – they were really welcoming and friendly. I knew that I would get the kind of support that I was looking for with my education. Also being able to talk to students already studying across all three years was super beneficial – they all talked really highly of the course and of UWTSD, so I knew I was in safe hands. What did you enjoy outside your studies? Outside of my studies I really enjoyed spending time outdoors. Carmarthen has a lot of lovely nature walks and two big parks. It’s also only a short drive from Llansteffan Beach, where groups of us would often spend the evening hanging out and exploring. I was also a member of the dance society on campus and that was always so much fun. It was a chance to socialise with people outside of your course, learn new skills and improve your fitness. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I am now working as a freelance actor and facilitator. I’m very lucky to have had some amazing opportunities within the industry since graduating. The BA Acting course taught me the importance of creating my own work, how to start from scratch and build/create something from nothing. The course had a huge influence on who I am now as a creative. I’m not just an actor, I’m a director, producer, and a theatre maker and that’s super important. I’ve filmed commercials, toured England with new writing, performed a one-woman show in Cardiff, built an installation, run workshops with students. I teach young children drama. I have an incredibly versatile career and that is due to my training at UWTSD. We focused on the industry as a whole and developed multiple different skills, building a little toolbox of all the things needed to thrive in the arts. What was your favourite thing about your course? My favourite thing about my course was the staff. My tutors were just incredible. The head of learning had a wealth of experience and knowledge relating to acting and the industry and we were able to meet and be taught by some really awesome people. I loved that some modules were taught by outside facilitators because, even though we were still studying, we were making connections and relationships with people in the industry, some of whom I have worked with since graduating. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I am a huge advocate for UWTSD and the BA Acting course. I could not recommend it enough. I absolutely adored my time studying, so much so that after two years I’m going back to study for a Master’s. It is such a welcoming campus and the staff really do care about your wellbeing. Everyone was always so helpful and attentive. Related Information Our Subjects Newsroom Open days and open evenings Previous slide Next slide

title: Celeste Turnbull - Acting (BA Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Celeste Turnbull - Acting (BA Hons) Celeste Turn
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Performance, Dance and Musical Theatre Student Stories Celeste Turnbull - Acting (BA Hons) Celeste Turnbull - Acting (BA Hons) Celeste's UWTSD Experience Name: Celeste Turnbull Course: BA (Hons) Acting Hometown: Burry Port Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Celeste's BA (Hons) Acting Experience What is your favourite thing about the Carmarthen campus? My favourite thing about the campus is the little nooks you can find during warmer weather to sit and do work in. These areas have helped me to relax and have helped to improve my focus and therefore my motivation to work. My favourite spot is near the large tree outside between the library and NIB001. I also found myself returning to this spot for mental wellbeing and general relaxation between classes. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD as it offered a primarily practical acting course, something which I could not find elsewhere. I am a practical and visual learner, therefore, this course has accommodated my needs and left me fulfilled and exceptional at my craft. I was also drawn to the number of opportunities that the acting course offered for me to perform in front of an audience. Audiences are what make theatre, so being able to experience this early on has reinforced my love for this industry. What do you enjoy outside your studies? Outside of my studies, I enjoy trips to Llansteffan beach with my friends, as well as taking long walks around Abergwili museum trail. Being able to drive has also allowed my friends and me to visit our local country park in Pembrey, only a 25-minute drive from campus! As someone who enjoys being active, Carmarthen Leisure Centre has been especially useful in helping me maintain my energy and motivation during each semester. There are also multiple castles nearby, which restore the history of our beautiful country! What do you hope to do when you graduate? Following graduation, I am hoping to do a master’s degree in Screen Acting! I then hope to enter the world of bilingual children’s television! Acting is my passion and is something I never thought I would get this far with. It poses challenges and pushes me to my extremes yet is a constant reminder to my younger self that it is possible to live your dreams!! What is your favourite thing about your course? My favourite thing about my course is the lecturers. Welcoming us each day with warm smiles and open hearts, supporting us as we strive to go beyond our comfort zones, and celebrating our achievements no matter how big or small, is only the foundation of the course. They treat us as an acting company rather than students and make us feel at one with them. They listen to, and consider any concerns we have, and are quick to implement feedback related to the course to make it a completely pleasant, enjoyable, and memorable experience for us all. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would recommend UWTSD to anyone in a heartbeat. During my time at UWTSD, I have had experience as a Student Ambassador, and was given the opportunity to study a semester abroad in California, where I found my love for rock climbing. This only enhanced my skillset and the attitude I approach each day with. Furthermore, through direct experience with the student services team, it is safe to say that my literary, as well as common skills have vastly improved, and have been shaped to guarantee further successes in future work. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Vinicius Dreher - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Vinicius Dreher - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Vinicius's UWTSD Experience Name: Vinicius Dreher Course: BEng Motorcycle Engineering Current Studies: PhD candidate Hometown: Sao Paulo Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Vinicius's BEng Motorcycle Engineering Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? I loved the opportunity to learn theoretical concepts in lectures and quickly test them in state-of-the-art facilities. The availability of a dyno engine, CNC, dyno rolling, and an excellent motorcycle workshop allowed for hands-on exploration and experimentation. The unique emphasis on motorcycles, combined with comprehensive training and access to cutting-edge resources, provided an unparalleled opportunity to delve deeply into this specialized field. My passion for motorcycles extends beyond my academic and professional life, enriching my personal life and hobbies. Additionally, I have co-founded a startup with another ex-UWTSD student, focusing on advanced motorcycle dynamics through a mobile application. Balancing family time, my start-up, and racing interests keeps me grounded and motivated. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I am currently pursuing a PhD at UWTSD, focusing on developing an intelligent motorcycle racing simulation platform. My bachelor’s degree in motorcycle engineering provided me with a solid foundation in both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, which have been crucial in advancing my academic and professional career. What was your favourite thing about your course? My favourite aspect of the course was the opportunity to dive deeply into the intricacies of motorcycle dynamics. As a motorcycle enthusiast, I found immense satisfaction in putting theoretical concepts to the test using advanced algorithms. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would highly recommend UWTSD because of its unique and specialized programmes, particularly in motorcycle engineering. title: Ragulan Pulanthitan - Automotive Engineering (BEng) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David

content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Ragulan Pulanthitan - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Ragulan Pulanthitan - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Ragulan's UWTSD Experience Name: Ragulan Pulanthitan Course: BEng Automotive Engineering Previous Studies: Ysgol Dyffryn Aman, Carmarthenshire (2015–2022); St. Luke’s Primary School, Dublin (2008–2015) Hometown: Place of Birth: The Hammocks, Miami-Dade Family Origins: Sri Lanka Current Residence: Ammanford, Carmarthenshire Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Ragulan's BEng Automotive Engineering Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The 24/7 computer room was relieving to have on campus as it was a useful room to do project and assignment work in. The MCR race team, as an extracurricular activity, was a large factor in why I chose to come to this institution. What did you enjoy outside your studies? The motorsport team is what I enjoy the most at UWTSD. I was able to gain the most amount of knowledge in first year from being a part of that team. Outside of the university, I enjoyed the experience of living in a city as it was a much-needed change of pace compared to where my family currently live. I think the combination of working in engineering whilst studying at UWTSD has been key to my progression and no doubt has helped me to get the job I have. I was able to learn the practical side of things whilst working at Consort (my old job) whilst the lecturers at UWTSD taught me the theoretical side of things, although they were very good at teaching us the topics in real life situations and applications too. What was your favourite thing about your course? My favourite thing about the course was learning in-depth information about various topics within Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would recommend UWTSD to anyone. The facilities are excellent, and the lecturers go above and beyond to help you. They supported me through my change of job. With the new job, it would have been challenging to continue my studies for the remaining 12 months of my course due to relocation to Paris in summer 2024. UWTSD allowed me to ‘fast track’ and complete all of my work by January 2024. This was invaluable to me. title: Ilias Iatrakis - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Ilias Iatrakis - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Ilias Iatrakis - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Ilias's U
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Ilias Iatrakis - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Ilias Iatrakis - Motorcycle Engineering (BEng) Ilias's UWTSD Experience Name: Ilias Iatrakis Course: MSc Motorcycle Engineering Previous Studies: BEng Motorcycle Engineering ; Technical Secondary Education in Industrial Sciences. (Or full A-Levels in STEM) Hometown: Genk, Belgium Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Ilias's MSc Motorcycle Engineering Experience What is your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The workshops including high-end technical facilities, available to the students to work on their projects of interest; the possibility to apply the theory we learn in class and being able to go into the workshop and perform the actual measurements and tests related to these subjects. I’ve had the privilege to run and ride for the University’s Motorcycle Racing project for two years. The current racing teams offer great opportunities related to development and competition, also allowing the students to gain real life experience in real paddocks, working on real projects. From machining to engine work, engine dynos, to suspension work, opportunities are there if you want them. Why did you choose UWTSD? In 2018, when I was 15, my father and I were choosing between UWTSD and a German university for my higher education. We visited UWTSD during an open day, and I was immediately impressed by the cutting-edge technology and equipment available. The highlight of our visit was meeting Dr Owen Williams, whose expertise and teaching approach greatly influenced our decision. The staff’s dedication and the university’s friendly atmosphere were also pivotal. Dr Owen’s commitment reassured us of the quality of education I would receive. Convinced, I decided to aim for enrolment at UWTSD, starting my journey towards turning my passion into knowledge. After just turning 17, I started the course in 2020. What do you enjoy outside your studies? I love staying active; whether it’s working out, exploring the outdoors, or mountain biking, I’m always on the move. Over the past two years, I’ve taken up surfing – a sport I now thoroughly enjoy in the beautiful nature of the Gower, which has become my favourite activity. However, my passion for motorcycles occupies much of my time outside of studies. I’m constantly engaged in racing, working on various projects, and experimenting with new ideas and concepts, all in the spirit of fun. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? Besides my Master’s in Motorcycle Engineering here at UWTSD, I’m currently working as a race engineer/ crew chief for MRP Racing in the BMW Motorrad Motorsport IDM Superbike team. When I graduate, I’m aiming to continue working in the racing paddock. I also aim to work within a development department in the automotive industry, with the end goal of a becoming a technical director of some sort. I’ve also got interest in opening my own ‘performance shop’, building and engineering race bikes. Besides the support of my parents, passion and continuous work towards my goals are the main driving factor. The knowledge we gain here is invaluable in the way it’s taught and is highly appreciated in the industry. What has been your favourite thing about your course? One of the major highlights for me has been the amount of hands-on opportunities and the sheer amount of specialised knowledge which the staff offers and shares with us. These experiences have allowed me, as a student, to engage in various professional activities related to motorcycles and racing. In particular, being given the opportunity to develop and ride for the university’s racing team has been an exceptional experience. Moreover, I had the privilege of eventually leading the team, which has undoubtedly been one of the most memorable and rewarding experiences of my young life. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would highly recommend this course to anyone interested in motorcycles or motorsport. I feel, and have noticed from established professionals, that the knowledge and opportunities you can get through this unique course can’t be gained elsewhere. The combination of specialised knowledge, the teaching method, hands-on opportunities, and the support of the University makes this course exceptional. I believe that pursuing this course would provide passionate individuals with a distinct advantage and a solid foundation for their future endeavours in this field. description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Max Hart - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Max Hart - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Max's UWTSD Experienc
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Max Hart - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Max Hart - Automotive Engineering (BEng) Max's UWTSD Experience Name: Max Hart Course: BEng Automotive Engineering Previous Studies: A-Levels in Maths, Physics, Product Design Hometown: Surrey Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Max's BEng Automotive Engineering Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The location! In Swansea you have the most amazing beaches, hills and countryside right on your doorstep. As well as this you have all the amenities you would expect in a big city, plus some fantastic bars and pubs, which is of course very important! The campus is close to the city centre so you’re never far away from everything Swansea has to offer. Why did you choose UWTSD? I looked around many unis and found that most felt quite sterile. Immediately I felt inspired by how enthusiastic everyone is at UWTSD; the lecturers are genuinely passionate about what they do and are very welcoming. The facilities on offer also impressed me, with lots of opportunities to participate in hands-on activities to support the theory learnt in lectures. What did you enjoy outside your studies? I enjoyed being a member of Team MCR (now Team MSport Eng). This allowed me to improve my practical skills and gain hands-on experience of working in a race team and competing at events all over the country. I was a student rep for my course and attended multiple outreach events at local schools on behalf of the University. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? After graduating, I started working as a Technical Sales Engineer for Diffusion – a commercial heating, air conditioning and ventilation (HVAC) manufacturer. I used the technical knowledge gained throughout my degree to help clients specify and design an HVAC solution to satisfy their specific requirements. I used previously learnt thermodynamic principles to calculate perform the required heating/cooling calculations. I recently moved into the defence industry, now working as a Systems Design Engineer for MBDA, a world leader in the manufacturing of defence equipment. Complex defence systems require a broad engineering skillset; experience from UWTSD of working with key engineering principles and tools, particularly MATLAB, whilst juggling multiple projects and sticking to strict deadlines helps me in the role hugely. What was your favourite thing about your course? Having the opportunity to work with like-minded, passionate people. Studying engineering, particularly automotive engineering, meant I was surrounded by people with the same interests as me. I made many close friends who I still see today. The lecturers share that enthusiasm and help achieve UWTSD’s uniquely personal and supportive learning style. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would always recommend UWTSD; I thoroughly enjoyed my time studying there. The skills I learnt allowed me to be where I am today, on the career path I have always wanted. title: Lucy Davies - Adventure Filmmaking (BA Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Film, Media and Animation Student Stories Lucy Davies - Adventure Filmmaking (BA Hons) Lucy Davies - Ad
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Film, Media and Animation Student Stories Lucy Davies - Adventure Filmmaking (BA Hons) Lucy Davies - Adventure Filmmaking (BA Hons) Lucy's UWTSD Experience Name: Lucy Davies Course: BA (Hons) Adventure Filmmaking Previous Studies: A-level: Photography, psychology, and physical education Hometown: Mumbles, Gower Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Lucy's BA (Hons) Adventure Filmmaking Experience What was your favourite thing about the Carmarthen campus? The location – the campus is not too far away from Gower or Pembrokeshire which are great locations for surfing and climbing and for shooting projects for this degree. The campus has loads of great facilities like the Mac labs and editing suites as well as the immersive room. It is also right next door to the S4C building which has provided us with loads of opportunities. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD for its unique degree. This university offered the only adventure filmmaking course I could find or the closest degree to the sort of career path I want to head down. I also like the fact that it is not a huge campus where you’re 1 of 300 in a class. You get a lot of help from lecturers and it feels like a tight-knit university where the lecturers can really give a lot of their time in lectures to help you. What did you enjoy outside your studies? Working with the outdoor adventure education degree students on lectures was great. I found people who also loved surfing and people who loved climbing. We would go out to places like Rhossili and abseil through caves or spend the day coasteering when we had spare time. I really enjoyed going out surfing and photographing my friends in the water. The expeditions were also amazing. There were opportunities to go on expeditions outside of lectures. We went on a climbing expedition to Spain in 2023 where we spent the week sport climbing and ascending cliffs with my camera to take photos of people climbing. We also went on a climbing expedition to Pembrokeshire and worked on our trad climbing skills and climbed multi-pitch trad routes overhanging the sea. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? The dream would be to make surf films or become a surf photographer but I would be really happy working in any areas related to adventure filmmaking. Working for the BBC Natural History Unit would be a dream come true or even National Geographic as a camera woman. I am currently working as a freelancer making documentaries for a nature reserve. I also work as a coasteering guide and rock-climbing instructor. In October or November, I will be flying out to Kalymnos, Greece to shoot an exciting project which will involve a bunch of rock climbers, riggers and a circus artist and stunt performer. I will likely be hanging 100ft off an overhanging cliff in my harness filming this stunt which I am really excited to do. What was your favourite thing about your course? The practical lectures. Some lectures we would be filming red kites with massive telephoto lenses and learning how to track them in flight and keep them in focus. Other lectures would be focusing on macro photography learning or learning how to focus stack. Some of our lectures were up in North Wales in December so we had opportunities to photograph people mountaineering in up to 6ft of snow up Crib Goch in Eryri. We also had opportunities to film and photograph the Pembrokeshire fire spinners multiple times, one of those times using RED cameras that cost up to £50,000. The practical lectures with the outdoor adventure education degree were also a highlight of this degree. We would go anywhere and everywhere either climbing, kayaking, mountaineering, or gaining first aid and catastrophic bleed qualifications. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? UWTSD feels like a close-knit university. The lecturers go above and beyond to help in any way they can. There are unique opportunities at this university like climbing expeditions abroad or filming and learning from some really successful people in the adventure filmmaking industry. The location of the campus is perfect for someone doing an adventure filmmaking degree. There is so much to offer in this part of the world for adrenaline junkies or wildlife photographers or anyone who loves the outdoors. title: Nathan Chaplin - Computer Games Design (BA Hons) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Film, Media and Animation Student Stories Nathan Chaplin - Computer Games Design (BA Hons) Nathan Chapl
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Film, Media and Animation Student Stories Nathan Chaplin - Computer Games Design (BA Hons) Nathan Chaplin - Computer Games Design (BA Hons) Nathan's UWTSD Experience Name: Nathan Chaplin Course: BA Computer Games Design Hometown: Baglan, Port Talbot Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Nathan's BA Computer Games Design Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? One of my favourite things about the campus would be the environment. Being on a creative course we used our day-to-day environments as inspiration to create new environments and experiences for players. Having the other departments around us allowed me to generate new unique ideas for my work. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD because of the experience the academics bring to the course and how they could help me reach my goals as a games designer. This gave me confidence, knowing no matter what I did, if that was failing or pushing the boundaries, that they would give me support and feedback so that I could get the best out of myself and the course. What did you enjoy outside your studies? I loved the social environment, being able to meet new people from other courses and go out to gain new experiences. One of the highlights was going to Insomnia with the team to not only have fun, but also to talk to game developers and ask for tips and tricks. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I am now working for UWTSD in the department Digital Creativity and Learning. My team is called Digital Experience and Engagement. I started here on a graduate role and now am full time and my role is VR Technology Specialist. I work on creating VR applications, Managing VR, Immersive Rooms, digital tours, drones and more. My course helped me get here by allowing me to experiment and push the boundaries on the technology we had. Without the course I would not feel confident in taking on new technologies and seeing what we can do with them. Looking back on some key areas I found the experience I gained from the academics was critical to my success so far. For this I am very grateful to all academics who taught me. What was your favourite thing about your course? It’s hard to decide as there are so many areas which I will always remember and so many highlights as without them I don’t think I would be doing what I do now. If I had to highlight one, it would be learning game history. As much as I push new and innovative technology, I think learning game history showed me how far technology has come and some of the hurdles people and companies have jumped through. I think it’s important to know the past to so you can help improve the future. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would recommend it 100% as not only does UWTSD have a range of courses to choose from but they also have some of the best academics, in my opinion, that can teach students a high level of skill in their area. From my experience the high level of the academics was really an inspiration. Also, the community that surrounds UWTSD is fantastic, they support you outside the classroom and there is always some experience or event to keep you entertained Related Information Our Subjects Newsroom Open days and open evenings Previous slide Next slide

content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Environment, Energy and Sustainability Student Stories Rebecca Macfarlane - Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (BSc) Rebecca Macfarlane - Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (BSc) Rebecca Macfarlane's UWTSD Experience Having a lot of outdoor hobbies, such as canicross, climbing, and caving, I chose to study BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change at UWTSD Swansea. Name: Rebecca Macfarlane Course: BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change Previous Studies: BA Philosophical Studies at UWTSD (though then it was University of Wales, Lampeter) Hometown: Llanelli Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Rebecca Macfarlane's BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The location – right by the sea made it easy to get outside and get some fresh air between classes, but it was also really close to the city centre if I ever needed anything. It was also easily accessible by car, which was particularly convenient for me as I was working full-time and would need to drive across the city to get to the office for certain days. Why did you choose UWTSD? The course content covered more of my interests whilst also keeping a focus on teaching employability skills. I was looking for a career change so it was important to me to find a course that had a good balance for delivering applicable learning without compromising on quality. It was also flexible enough that I could continue to work full-time after consultation with my employer. What did you enjoy outside your studies? Alongside canicross, caving, and climbing, I practice a lot of martial arts, such as lau gar, kendo and tai chi. Admittedly my focus on them dropped slightly the further I got into my final year, but I’m looking forward to getting stuck back in again. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I’m in the process of following through with my career change plans, and recently accepted a graduate environmental scientist position with Welsh Water. This wouldn’t have been possible without the course, so I’m immensely grateful for the opportunity. Additionally, I’m hoping to continue my studies by pursuing a PhD that continues the research I performed for my dissertation. What was your favourite thing about BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change? The mixture of fieldwork and lab sessions gave a good overview of what it would be like to pursue a range of careers, and the opportunity to learn or refine practical skills was always offered. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? Definitely – everyone goes above and beyond to support you throughout your studies, and you’re always invited to present your views, or just have a chat. description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Environment, Energy and Sustainability Student Stories Rowan Jack Moses - Environment, Sustainability a
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Environment, Energy and Sustainability Student Stories Rowan Jack Moses - Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (BSc) Rowan Jack Moses - Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (BSc) Student Name's UWTSD Experience Hi, I’m Rowan! I study Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change in Swansea. I’m passionate about environmental communication and education. Name: Rowan Jack Moses (They/Them pronouns) Course: BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change Previous Studies: Horticulture Apprenticeship at the National Botanic Garden of Wales and the Royal Horticultural Society. Hometown: Ammanford, Carmarthenshire Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Rowan's BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change Experience What is your favourite thing about Swansea campus? I study at the SA1 Waterfront Campus, and I love how close to the sea it is. I’ve seen seals on my walk into uni, and my favourite seat in the library gives me a view over the ocean while I’m studying! Why did you choose UWTSD? I wanted to study close enough to my family to visit often, as I have a young sister. I also wanted a Welsh university that engages with Welsh environmental issues, as these are so often overlooked in the wider UK context. A university with good disability support was also vital, as I am Autistic and ADHD, and I’d heard good things about the quality of support available. What do you hope to do when you graduate? I want to work in environmental communication and engagement, ideally increasing access to nature and environmental spaces and knowledge for marginalised groups such as disabled and LGBTQ+ people. What do you enjoy outside your studies? I love Swansea! I live here year round with my partner, and we’ve found there’s a lovely local community. Places like the Environment Centre are really good for getting involved in local environmental action, and venue spaces such as Elysium always have interesting creative events. What is your favourite thing about BSc Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change? The course covers a really broad range of topics, which I’ve really enjoyed and benefited from. At the same time, you can easily focus on your particular interests for assignments, using different lenses to examine your interests throughout the course. There are lots of opportunities for practical engagement, and all the lecturers are really supportive. One of my favourite trips we went on, we got to see wind turbines that hadn’t been put up yet. It was really cool to see them up close, and how large they are! Would you recommend UWTSD and why? Being disabled, the smaller campus and class sizes make it possible for me to attend university. It’s very personal, people know you and what you’re up to; you’re not just a face in the crowd. Related Information Our Subjects Newsroom Open days and open evenings Previous slide Next slide

title: Milena Tomaszewska - Energy and Environmental Engineering (BEng) | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Environment, Energy and Sustainability Student Stories Milena Tomaszewska - Energy and Environmental En
content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Environment, Energy and Sustainability Student Stories Milena Tomaszewska - Energy and Environmental Engineering (BEng) Milena Tomaszewska - Energy and Environmental Engineering (BEng) Milena's UWTSD Experience Name: Milena Tomaszewska Course: BEng Energy and Environmental Engineering Previous Studies: A-levels and GCSEs at Morriston Comprehensive School Hometown: Swansea since 2013; previously Wroclaw, Poland Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Milena's BEng Energy and Environmental Engineering Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The IQ building, it’s modern with many ‘chill-out’ spaces, providing comfort during stressful times. The cafeterias were always lively with familiar faces – whether peers, lecturers, or friendly staff. The welcoming environment made it easy to relax and connect. I loved the state-of-the-art engineering equipment and often spent free periods exploring the labs, fascinated by the technology in action. Why did you choose UWTSD? In sixth form, I was unsure about my future and career path, fluctuating between fields like criminology, nursing, and veterinary science. My teacher suggested UWTSD for its blend of theory and practical experience. The hands-on learning approach, combined with lecturers who had real industry experience, made UWTSD the perfect choice for me. What did you enjoy outside your studies? To maintain my mental and physical health, I joined Swansea Sirens at Swansea University. It was great to collaborate with Swansea University for sports while studying my chosen course. I also nurtured my side hustle, which has since grown into two successful businesses. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? After my BEng, I pursued a master’s in Computer Science to stay current with technological advancements. Now nearing the end of my master’s, I’ve accepted a graduate role in sales at City Science. Surprisingly, this role combines my engineering, IT, marketing, and business skills from both studies and entrepreneurship, making it an unexpected yet perfect fit for my career. What was your favourite thing about your course? The lecturers’ passion and real-world industry insights were invaluable. They shared stories – funny, challenging, happy, and sad – that provided a deep understanding of the profession. A field trip to CAE, organised by my lecturer, was a highlight. It was not only educational but also inspired my dissertation on sustainability, blending theory with practical experience and encouraging personal growth and creative thinking. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would recommend UWTSD for those who value smaller class sizes and direct interaction with lecturers. The university offers ample opportunities for questions and discussions, fostering a supportive and engaging learning environment. There’s also strong support for securing internships. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Computing Student Stories Francois Riches - CertHE in STEM (Computing) Francois Riches - CertHE in STEM (Computing) Francois's UWTSD Experience Name: Francois Riches Course: Certificate in Higher Education Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (Computing) Hometown: Port Talbot Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Francois's CertHE Stem (Computing) Experience What is your favourite thing about Swansea campus? My favourite thing about attending the IQ Building for my studies is often the walk there in the mornings. The views of the marina to one side and the green hills on the other are often a great start to the day. It can be a really refreshing walk before arriving at the IQ early and making myself comfortable. The library is right next door and has some great views too. It might seem like a small thing, but anything that can help in keeping a good positive mindset I find quite important. Why did you choose UWTSD? To be entirely honest it was proximity – living in Port Talbot it was simply easier to attend UWTSD. Not that I had even considered anywhere else. I only have UWTSD for reference but I’m very happy there and I look forward to the rest of my time studying there. What do you enjoy outside your studies? Mostly as a mature student I enjoy the people in my life and my solitude sitting at my computer. A little bit of gaming at home and time with friends and their families. I am also involved with a local charity and enjoy volunteering with them. I like eating out and getting coffee in Swansea. What do you hope to do when you graduate? I am taking everything one step at a time and have not given much thought to what comes after university. I have received emails that inform me of events for employment and other opportunities held at UWTSD. I’m yet to attend one of these since I am only at foundation level, however, next year I plan to partake and see what is available. For me personally the journey is enough right now; I’ll let the destination reveal itself. What is your favourite thing about your course? I have enjoyed a lot about attending the course, and it is hard to single out just one thing. I have had many great lecturers at the University, many different and interesting personalities for the most part excellent at keeping me engaged and interested. I’ve enjoyed working with my peers, being helped by them and helping others. As a mature student I have even enjoyed just the academic journey, the challenge to myself to actually do something constructive. And I really enjoyed getting to do that in a comfortable and welcoming environment. How has the course helped you? Attending the course has helped me a great deal. I had no structure before this, and it really helps by engaging me intellectually. The CertHE foundation course in particular helps with my lack of knowledge concerning academic standards. From how to effectively write reports, to mathematics and programming, I feel better prepared for the degree ahead of me. It has also given me needed experience in taking exams and giving presentations. Related Information Our Subjects Newsroom Open days and open evenings Previous slide Next slide

content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Civil Engineering, Construction and Architecture Student Stories Jon Langstone - Construction Management (BSc Hons) Jon Langstone - Construction Management (BSc Hons) Jon's UWTSD Experience Name: Jon Langstone Course: BSc(Hons) Construction Management Previous Studies: Engineering and Stonemasonry Hometown: Swansea Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Jon's BSc Construction Management Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? The campus was in an ideal location for me, by the sea front, easily accessible to bike routes that stretch all the way to Mumbles from SA1. Also, the facilities were always kept clean, and the library. Why did you choose UWTSD? I chose UWTSD because I read that they had small classes, the staff had experience in the field that I was studying to pursue a career in (Construction), and the chances of securing a graduate role after graduating were quite high. I found all of this to be correct. What did you enjoy outside your studies? As a single parent, my spare time outside my studies were mainly taken up by frequent dog walks, lots of cooking, and plenty of reading. What are you doing now, how did you get to where you are and how has your course helped you in your career? I secured a graduate position at a multifaceted engineering and project management construction consultancy company, based in Cardiff. I am thoroughly enjoying my new role as a graduate project manager at Burroughs. I am responsible for actively supporting the project management team and subsequent engineering teams in successfully delivering large and complex projects across the UK and sometimes beyond – which is exactly what I was hoping to do, prior to graduating. The course that I undertook at UWTSD gave me the foundational skills that I needed to help me focus on learning the detailed information needed to excel in my role. Even a year on, the lecturers who I developed a relationship with are still able to answer the odd query that I have. Specifically, I found that the staff at UWTSD are very good at preparing undergraduates to go out into their chosen industries with confidence and excitement. What was your favourite thing about your course? I personally enjoyed how personal the course was overall. The small class sizes allowed me to question my lecturers more easily, which then helped me learn a lot more information, as opposed to a more individual-based learning structure. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? I would highly recommend UWTSD, especially to anyone thinking about getting involved in the construction industry. Each lecturer I had took a different approach to teaching and a set of different skills, which allowed me to preview different types of professional routes through the construction industry, before jumping in after graduation. content: Home Experience and Facilities Student Stories Civil Engineering, Construction and Architecture Student Stories Drew Dennehy - Architecture (BSc Hons) Drew Dennehy - Architecture (BSc Hons) Drew's UWTSD Experience Name: Drew Dennehy Course: BSc Architecture Previous Studies: City & Guilds Plumbing and Heating Level 2; City & Guilds Plumbing and Heating Level 3 Hometown: Bridgwater Book an Open Day Order a Prospectus Drew's BSc Architecture Experience What was your favourite thing about Swansea campus? Studying in the IQ campus I would say the library was my favourite thing. I spent a lot of time in there looking over the architectural magazines that UWTSD subscribes to and flicking through books for inspiration for my projects. Why did you choose UWTSD? I came through the apprenticeship route and heard about UWTSD through a previous employer. I contacted UWTSD and they gave me a chance. The way we were taught was brilliant and I would recommend the course to anyone. What did you enjoy outside your studies? The course was demanding, requiring a lot of my time and effort to produce work I was proud of. However, when I did set time aside for other things, it was spending time with flatmates. Bowling, going out, BBQs on the beach – we enjoyed the time that we had throughout our years together at UWTSD. What do you hope to do when you graduate? The plan is to move to Edinburgh to begin my Part 2. It is a beautiful city that I have always been fond of; however, there is currently a shortage of jobs in Scotland as a whole so I have opened myself up to working wherever there is an opportunity. But I am set on proceeding with my journey in architecture so I can move on to my Masters. What was your favourite thing about your course? The level of one-to-one time with lecturers is something that none of my friends experienced in other universities. There is a healthy level of competition where everyone wants to produce the best work they can but if someone discovers a new technique they still share it amongst their peers, rather than keep it to themselves. Over the last three years, we have all become close and gotten to know each other well. Seeing how they have each individually developed has got to be one of the greatest highlights for me. Would you recommend UWTSD and why? For sure, the lecturers are a credit to the course and prepare students for practice much more than alternative universities. We study the business and technical aspects of design as well as the aesthetics which allows us to offer more to employers than other students might be able to. The tutors are always looking at how we can develop the course and value student feedback. The lecturers were also easily accessible in person and over the phone. content: Home Experience and Facilities Sport External Sports Venues External Sports Venues Exploring outside of UWTSD Sport is a big part of the culture of Wales and going to see an event or match is an essential part of studying at UWTSD. Check out the several venues below which you can visit whenever you wish to. Swansea Swansea.com Stadium The Swansea.com Stadium opened in 2005 to provide a home to Swansea City and Ospreys Rugby while giving Swansea a facility to be proud of. Swansea Bay Sports Park Facilities at Swansea Bay Sports Park range from the 50m Wales National Pool Swansea, an outdoor athletics track, multi-use pitches, gym, hockey pitches and much more. St. Helen’s Rugby & Cricket Ground St. Helen’s Rugby and Cricket Ground is a sports venue in Swansea, home of Swansea Rugby Football Club, Swansea Cricket Club and Glamorgan Cricket. Parc y Scarlets Home of Scarlets Rugby and a fantastic venue for all manner of conferences, occasions and celebrations. Machynys Golf Course, Llanelli Machynys, which translates to ‘Monks Island’, is a Nicklaus-designed 7121-yard modern links championship golf course opening in 2005, which has already hosted an unprecedented 14 Championships. Please note that these external facilities are not free to use, you will be subject to a service charge when using them. Cardiff Principality Stadium Sporting the first fully retractable roof in the UK, the Principality Stadium in Cardiff is at the leading edge as a multi-purpose, multi-faceted event venue, home of the Welsh Rugby Union. Sophia Gardens Sophia Gardens is a 16,000-seater stadium in Cardiff, home of Glamorgan Cricket and an established venue for international cricket. Cardiff City Stadium The Cardiff City Stadium is the home of Cardiff City Football Club and the Wales national football team. Cardiff Arms Park Cardiff Arms Park is the home of Cardiff Rugby and Cardiff RFC situated next to the Principality Stadium in the heart of the Welsh capital. International Sports Village Bordering the freshwater lake created by Cardiff Bay Barrage, the Sports Village already boasts two Olympic standard sporting facilities, Cardiff International White Water and Cardiff International Pool. Alongside these, you will find the Viola Arena - which is both a public skating rink and home of the Cardiff Devils Elite League ice hockey team. Please note that these external facilities are not free to use, you will be subject to a service charge when using them. Carmarthen Ffos Las Racecourse Ffos Las Racecourse has brought top-class racing to Wales since it opened in 2009. Settled in between Llanelli and Carmarthen, Ffos Las hosts 23 racing fixtures across the year, as well as being available for hire for conferences and events. Richmond Park, Carmarthen Richmond Park is a Welsh Premier League stadium in Carmarthen. Situated on Priory Street, it is currently used for football matches and is the home ground of Carmarthen Town AFC. Carmarthen Park Opened in 1900, Carmarthen Park boasts Wales’s first velodrome (cycle track) and one of the few early velodromes to survive in working condition. Complete with its original grandstand, bandstand, lodge, entrance gates, and railings, Carmarthen Park has been used for a wide range of sports, eisteddfodau, entertainment, circuses, and concerts. Cynefin The UWTSD Centre for Outdoor Adventure Education Cynefin sits on a magnificent green site on the outskirts of Carmarthen, just 20 minutes’ walk from campus. The site is sheltered and secluded with a diverse range of natural habitats and access to waterways and footpaths. The centre’s location is perfect for learning about outdoor adventure education. title: Health and Physical Literacy Research | University of Wales Trinity Saint David
description: Home Study Experience and Facilities Sport Health and Physical Literacy Research Health and Physical Literacy Research Introduction Our work at the Wa
content: Home Study Experience and Facilities Sport Health and Physical Literacy Research Health and Physical Literacy Research Introduction Our work at the Wales Academy for Health and Physical Literacy (WAHPL) is grounded in a Saluto-ecological approach, combining McElroy’s adaptation of Bronfenbrenner’s Social Ecological Model with Antonovsky’s Salutogenesis. We view physical literacy as both a personal resource for lifelong physical activity and a foundation for broader wellbeing (Piper et al., 2022). Our research spans the life course - from early childhood and parenting to ageing populations - and is embedded in practice. We also support Post-graduate Research studies at both Master’s and PhD levels linked to Health and Physical Literacy. Post-Graduate Taught Programmes We have a range of completed and on-going post graduate research studies linked to Health and Physical Literacy. Outdoor Education, MA (Part-time) Sport and Exercise Nutrition, MSc / PG-Dip (Part-time) Physical Education, Sport and Physical Literacy, MA (Part-time) Student research projects from these PG programmes have investigated a range of topics. Some examples include: Outdoor Education, MA -Dissertation Research An exploration of how women perceive the presence of others to affect their freedom in outdoor activities. The landscape of outdoor learning in Zimbabwe and the impact of indigenous culture on engagement with the outdoors. ‘Sense of Place’ in Further Education Outdoor Adventure. How does disconnection from social media on a three-day, UK-based, outdoor residential contribute to the learning experience and change in attitudes or behaviour toward future use? Sharing the experience: parent perspectives of an outdoor education programme for families with children and young persons at an SEN school. Paddlesport motivation within Wales: an exploration of motivational differences for recreational Paddlesport participation within Wales. Physical Literacy and Physical Education, MA - Dissertation Research Parental perspectives in relation to pre-schoolers physical activity Opportunities for female-identifying-players in Ultimate Parents’ perception of early specialisation The impact of SKIP-Cymru on pupils’ motor skills The role of street dance in interest development and subjective task value of male secondary students Psychosocial and environmental factors that influence university students’ physical activity. PhD and Postgraduate Research Current PhD Projects: Alan Samual (ongoing) - The evaluation of a mobile application aimed at improving how parents support fundamental movement skills in their children. Tara Crank (ongoing) - Exploring the potential of digital technologies for supporting Nature Connection in Wellbeing Courses at a Community Green Health Hub. Wendy Scott (ongoing) - Exploring whether synchronising exercise type and intensity to menstrual cycle phases can be effective in improving perimenopause related symptoms, mood state and physiological health. Completed PhD Projects: Dr Amanda John: The impact of SKIP Cymru professional development on pupils’ motor competence, perceived competence and physical activity. Dr. Kate Piper: A social ecological study of mass participation sports events in Pembrokeshire. Dr Anna Stevenson: The evaluation and development of Footie Families, a family engagement motor skill programme. Dr David Gardner: High Intensity Training for post-menopausal women Dr Graham French: A new model for Outdoor Adventure Education for Key Stage 3 Dr Martin Norman: Therapeutic landscapes Contact us for more information about studying at postgraduate level Early Childhood Research We have a range of published research in the field of early childhood physical development. SKIP Cymru A three-year EU-funded PhD research project led to the development of more in-depth accredited professional development across this programme. Footie Families Recent research examined the perceptions and needs of parents in relation to their pre-school children’s physical activity. The result of this was the development of the Footie Families early years engagement programme in collaboration with the Football Association of Wales (FAW). MiniMovers Working in collaboration with ATiC we have researched the impact of the MiniMovers APP activities on pre-schoolers’ physical development and the experiences of parents. Contact us about our Physical Literacy research Access our publications Outdoor Research Outdoor Research at WAHPL At the Wales Academy of Health and Physical Literacy (WAHPL), our outdoor research is shaping new understanding in the fields of education, physical literacy, and health. We explore how outdoor and nature-based activities can significantly enhance physical and mental wellbeing across all stages of life. From early years to later life, outdoor experiences are a vital part of developing physical literacy. Young children may explore nature through Forest School settings or family adventures.
